newsitem.title: USA: Russia has IBM supercomputer for nuclear tests-NYT.
newsitem.headline: Russia has IBM supercomputer for nuclear tests-NYT.

text.p: Russian officials say their nuclear weapons establishment has obtained an IBM supercomputer through a European middleman, circumventing U.S. export controls, the New York Times reported on Tuesday.
Russian officials told the paper they planned to use the computer, an IBM RS/6000 SP bought for $7 million, to simulate nuclear tests.

U.S. laws restrict the export of high-tech computers that could be used for military purposes. The report about the IBM computer coincides with a separate investigation into whether two supercomputer systems sold to Russia by Silicon Graphics Inc are being used for nuclear testing.
Silicon Graphics said in a statement last week it had believed high-powered computers it shipped to a Russian laboratory in 1996 were for environmental research.
The California company also said it was cooperating with the Department of Commerce to determine if the systems had been diverted for inappropriate use.

Tuesday's report said U.S. laws required American computer makers to consult with the Commerce Department before selling Russia any computer that can perform between two billion and seven billion calculations a second.
The report quoted Russian officials as saying the IBM computer they obtained could perform 10 billion calculations a second and was 10 times more effective than the computers they now have.
It said Russian officials declined to reveal which middleman sold them the IBM computer.
"If we see something we can buy on the European market, we buy it," Vladislav Petrov, head of the public affairs department for Russia's Ministry of Atomic Energy Affairs told the paper.
